input: Most of my day was spent pulling together a cohesive view of our Q1 performance and answering ad-hoc questions from leadership. I consolidated data from our billing system, product analytics, and CRM to build a single dashboard that shows MRR growth, churn broken down by segment, and feature adoption for the last major release. I also investigated a question from the CEO about why our activation rate dipped in March despite higher top-of-funnel signups; after slicing the data by acquisition channel, I found that a new paid campaign was bringing in lower-intent users who churn within the first week. I documented this in a short memo with charts and suggested pausing or tweaking that campaign. I’m blocked on getting clear definitions for a couple of metrics we want to track in Q2 (specifically ‘engaged account’ vs ‘engaged user’), and I’ve scheduled a working session with Product and Sales to align. My intent tomorrow is to finalize the Q1 review deck, publish the new dashboard to the leadership workspace, and define a small set of north-star and supporting metrics that we can track consistently going forward.

input: Maya (Product Designer, Web): “Most of the day went into iterating on the new onboarding flow based on yesterday’s usability test recordings. I went through all eight sessions and tagged moments where users hesitated, especially on the workspace setup and teammate invite screens. The main friction points were ambiguous copy around ‘Organization Name’ vs ‘Project Name’ and a cluttered role selection component that surfaced all advanced permissions up front. I redesigned that part of the flow with a much simpler ‘Recommended setup’ path and moved advanced role customization behind a clearly labeled ‘Configure later’ link. I also updated the Figma prototype to include a progress indicator that clearly shows users they’re on step 2 of 3, which came up as a big reassurance factor in the tests. I’m slightly blocked because I need engineering input on whether we can technically support inline validation for company domain verification in step 1, or if that would require another backend service. input: Esha (iOS Engineer): “Today I tackled a long-standing crash bug and made progress on our offline caching strategy. The crash was happening sporadically when users returned to the app after a long time in the background; after instrumenting additional logging and analyzing crash reports, I traced it to a race condition between a token refresh call and a protected API request. I fixed it by centralizing token refresh logic, ensuring that only one refresh operation can run at a time, and queuing dependent requests until the refresh completes. On the offline caching front, I implemented a local data store using Core Data to persist recently viewed projects and tasks, and added a simple ‘last synced’ indicator in the UI. I’m partially blocked by backend constraints, since not all APIs currently support incremental sync, and I’ve opened a conversation with the backend team about adding updated_at filters. My intent tomorrow is to write unit tests around the token refresh logic, expand offline support to include comments, and work with Product on clear error copy for when users try to perform unsupported actions while offline.”

decisions: Centralized token refresh logic
Implemented local data store

input: Gaurav (Android Engineer): “Most of my day went into refactoring the navigation stack in the Android app to support the new ‘multi-workspace’ feature. Our existing implementation assumed a single active workspace, which made deep linking into specific projects brittle and error-prone. I migrated core screens to use the Navigation Component with safe args, set up a proper graph that reflects the new hierarchy (workspace → project → task), and updated our deep link handlers to parse the workspace ID from incoming URLs. I also added basic instrumentation so we can see how often users switch workspaces and which paths they use to navigate. I’m currently blocked on design specs for a couple of edge cases, like what happens when a user opens a deep link to a workspace they no longer have access to; I’ve left comments in the Figma file. My intent tomorrow is to finish QAing the navigation changes on a variety of devices, write a small internal doc for the team explaining the new patterns, and then pick up the follow-up tasks for supporting cross-workspace search before the beta launch on 28th April.”
